about: Every tool under tools/: its category (the folder it lives in), the question it answers, how it is run and its tests. An instrument carries a real output sample from this machine and how to read it; tools/README.md is written from this file by tools/checks/check-catalog.mjs --write, and check:boundaries holds the two to each other and to the tree.

tools.question: Does a title run in a browser, and what did the run do?
tools.sample:
The Swapper undefined -- TheSwapper.exe
  ran for 13ms, 4 guest instructions
stopped: exited with 3221225477
errors -- what the engine did not do:
  mscoree.dll!_CorExeMain: not implemented, answered with nothing
1 imports nothing claimed:
  mscoree.dll  (1)
tools.source: tools/cdp_test/reports/game-2026-11-14T03-28-29-645Z.txt (a run of steam-231160 without its .NET runtime; it printed "undefined" for the missing version, which the title line now leaves out)
tools.read: The first lines are how the run ended (exit 0xC0000005 here); "errors" and "imports nothing claimed" are what the engine lacked, the first thing to implement. The rest of a report is the address space, the last host calls and, with flags, profiles and frames.

tools.command: node tools/run/install-watch.mjs <setup.exe | disc.iso | archive.zip> | --bundle ID [--which PATH] [--args ARGS]

tools.question: Which guest instructions does a run execute most, what does each kind cost, and how do its calls go?
tools.sample:
114795 blocks, 5435328071 instructions in TheSwapper.exe, clr.dll@0x2dea000, 1082654156 block executions outside them
share  ops-share  ops/insn  form
  9.6%      14.1%        48  push r32
  3.3%       9.7%        95  mov m32,r32
  4.0%       7.2%        59  call rel
  4.8%       7.0%        48  jne rel
tools.read: share is of the executed instructions, ops-share of the wasm operations they cost, ops/insn what one form costs: a form whose ops-share is far above its share (push stack32, 147 ops) is where the translator spends. --calls prints the calls' shape as JSON (direct, indirect, import; registers live around them).

tools.question: What machine code, wasm text or wasm bytes does a region become, weighed by how often it ran?
tools.command: node tools/translator/cork-asm.mjs --image DLL@BASE | --bin FILE --at A --entry A [--blocks FILE] [--classes|--wat|--expansion]
tools.sample:
entry  blocks  x86  wasm B  machine  bytes  per x86  ran x86  weighted
0x00401160      43  229   11492     3297  15122    14.40       9M      2.94
ran: 0.01 G guest instructions in these blocks, 2.940 machine instructions an executed one
by kind, an executed guest instruction: other 0.935 (31.8%), branch 0.606 (20.6%), memory 0.444 (15.1%), compare 0.395
tools.read: "per x86" is machine instructions a guest instruction becomes in the code as compiled; "weighted" the same over what ran. The kinds line says where the instructions go besides the guest's own work (branch, memory, frame spills). The host here is arm64 (this VM).

tools.question: What does translating cost, to the instruction: a pass, its forming and emitting, and the price of a region, a block, a call and any other instruction?
tools.command: node tools/translator/emit-count.mjs --qemu DIR [--root DIR]... [--regions N] [--warm W] [--reps R]
tools.sample:
<base>: 2042.4 M instructions a pass of work (forming 474.1, emitting 1568.3), passes 2018.9..2086.7; compiles 104.3 a pass; 306 regions, 2657564 wasm bytes
  forming  price list (R^2 0.901, a region's error 25.9% at the median): region -59.8k (-4%), block -5.9k (-10%), call 116.5k (57%), ret 163.1k (14%), jmp 32.5k (7%), other 7.0k (36%)
  emitting price list (R^2 0.978, a region's error 10.8% at the median): region 313.1k (6%), block 15.1k (8%), call 152.2k (23%), ret 222.2k (6%), jmp -0.5k (-0%), other 36.6k (57%)
<helper lookup by looks>: 1915.8 M instructions a pass of work (forming 341.3, emitting 1574.5), passes 1891.4..1964.1; compiles 104.3 a pass; 306 regions, 2657564 wasm bytes; 0.9380 of the first
tools.source: emit-count.mjs --qemu <qemu 8.2.2 built with plugins> --root <1851609d> --root <its helperAt keyed by looks> --regions 10 --warm 15 --reps 3, node 22.22.0
tools.read: "work" is what a pass costs without V8's optimising compiles, whose moments jump from pass to pass; it is the same in every run of a tree, and arms are compared by it ("of the first"); "passes" is the spread of the counted passes. The price lists are least squares over every region's own count: what one more region, block (with the jump that ends it), call, return, jump or other instruction costs in machine instructions, and its share of the part. Forming's fit is loose (its cost hangs on what the shared decoding already found); emitting's is close: the cost is the sum of those prices, nothing growing with a region's size. A negative price is a term the others absorb.

tools.question: What does translated code cost to run, to the instruction an iteration and for each of the guest's own instructions, workload by workload and arm against arm?
tools.command: node tools/translator/run-count.mjs --qemu DIR [--root DIR]... [--bits 32|64|both] [--warm N] [--iters N] [--arm64 NODE [--sysroot DIR] [--lib DIR] [--node-flags FLAGS]] [workload...]
tools.sample:
instructions an iteration (100 warm, 20 counted), in square brackets a guest instruction's cost in them, arms: <657107ac>, <657107ac>
  str-32                   2555529 [2.549]  2555529 [2.549] (1.0000)
  switch-32                545575 [2.209]  545575 [2.209] (1.0000)
  vcall-32                 2076236 [4.414]  2076236 [4.414] (1.0000)
<657107ac>: geomean 1.0000 of the first
dearest first (the last arm): vcall-32 4.41, str-32 2.55, switch-32 2.21
tools.source: run-count.mjs --bits 32 str switch vcall under qemu 8.2.2 with tools/lib/qemu-count.c, node 26.13.1, one tree (cork 657107ac, 2026-11-15) as both arms of one run. Two runs started together agree to the instruction; separate runs of a tree agree to a few hundredths of a per cent on these and differ by a few per cent on load (V8's optimising compiles land when the machine has them done). The calls512 and calls4096 workloads call each callee 64 times an iteration, and V8 leaves a callee in its baseline code for some nine thousand calls: at the default --warm 100 their count is of baseline callees (calls512 on arm64 28.5 a guest instruction at warm 400, 9.4 at warm 2000) - give them --warm 2000. An arm64 host is counted with --arm64 (an arm64 node 26.13.1 under qemu-aarch64 8.2.2, --node-flags --no-wasm-bounds-checks for V8 as on macOS, --warm 400): str-32 2.270, switch-32 2.343, vcall-32 3.735 a guest instruction on cork 14eff061 (2026-11-17)
tools.read: Each cell is the instructions an iteration of the counted ones took, the whole process but V8's optimising compiles; the square bracket is that count over the guest's own instructions in the iteration - a processor running the image takes 1 - and the round bracket the arm's count against the first. A tree counts the same in every run, so a ratio off 1.0000 is the change's - except on a workload that keeps translating (load), which varies by a few per cent between separate runs: read it over several. The geomean is over the workloads shown; the last line orders them by a guest instruction's cost, the dearest first.

tools.question: What does one of a program's own instructions cost once its code has settled, with the whole app around it and the machine's time taken out, arm against arm?
tools.command: node tools/translator/pe-count.mjs --qemu DIR [--root DIR]... [--variant x87|sse|x64] [--from MILLIONS] [--to MILLIONS] [--cork JSON] [--arm64 NODE [--sysroot DIR] [--lib DIR] [--node-flags FLAGS]] workload...
tools.sample:
machine instructions a guest instruction between 150 and 250 million of the guest's (in V8's code, then the whole process but V8's optimising compiles), arms: <657107ac>, <657107ac>
  entities-sse     7.2629 7.3135 [115 regions, 0 formed again, 0 callees]  7.2629 7.3135 (1.0000) [115 regions, 0 formed again, 0 callees]
tools.source: pe-count.mjs --variant sse --from 150 --to 250 entities under qemu 8.2.2 with tools/lib/qemu-count.c, node 26.13.1, one tree (cork 657107ac, 2026-11-15) as both arms. An early window, taken for the sample's length: no callee is formed in yet. The settled windows of that tree: entities-sse 2800-2900 million 4.2225 4.2459 (5 formed again, 24 callees), spread-x87 1200-1300 million 4.1643 4.1926, each twice the same to the last digit
tools.read: Each arm's first figure is machine instructions in V8's code (the translated code, cork's runtime, the app) over the guest instructions of the window, the second the whole process but V8's optimising compiles, the round bracket that against the first arm; a processor running the program takes 1. The square bracket says where the translator was at the second mark: its regions, how many it formed again with callees, the most callees one call has formed in - a window with regions still being formed again is not settled. Both marks are in one run and the run is on a closed clock (tools/lib/closed-clock.mjs), so one tree gives the same figures every time; the counts taken before this tool as the difference of two runs on the machine's clock differed by a tenth on one tree.

tools.question: How much resident memory does a translated module cost past its bytes, compiled lazily, by the baseline compiler or by the optimising one?
tools.sample:
node v26.13.1 (defaults): 837 modules, 9.6 MiB of wasm; resident +15.5 MiB, 1.62 times their bytes
node v26.13.1 --no-wasm-lazy-compilation --no-wasm-tier-up: 837 modules, 9.6 MiB of wasm; resident +35.9 MiB, 3.75 times their bytes
node v26.13.1 --no-wasm-lazy-compilation --no-liftoff: 837 modules, 9.6 MiB of wasm; resident +58.3 MiB, 6.09 times their bytes
tools.source: module-memory.mjs under node 26.13.1 (V8 14.6) with each set of flags, the micro benchmark's first 40 regions of each image
tools.read: The multiple is what holding a module costs over its wasm bytes: lazily compiled, nothing has run; the other two lines are every function compiled by Liftoff or TurboFan. A program pays the first for every module and between the other two for what ran. Resident memory moves by a few per cent run to run.

tools.question: Which function of a system or runtime DLL is hot?
tools.sample:
48991 public symbols; the image 55.6% of 2436222218 block executions
  2.11%  ?mark_object_simple1@gc_heap@WKS@@KGXPAE@Z
  1.68%  ?relocate_address@gc_heap@WKS@@KGXPAPAE@Z
  1.43%  ?relocate_survivors_in_plug@gc_heap@WKS@@KGXPAE0PAUrelocate_args@12@@Z
  1.41%  ?FillEntryDataForAncestor@MethodDataObject@MethodTable@@IAEXPAV2@@Z
tools.read: The image's share of the run's block executions, then its public functions by share: here the CLR's garbage collector (mark, relocate) leads The Swapper's ngen load.

tools.question: What is the code at module+offset, as a profile names it?
tools.sample:
== clr.dll+0xb5a08
  000b5a08  8d65f4               lea      esp, [ebp - 0xc]
  000b5a0b  5f                   pop      edi
  000b5a0c  5e                   pop      esi
  000b5a0d  8b4dfc               mov      ecx, dword ptr [ebp - 4]
  000b5a10  33cd                 xor      ecx, ebp
tools.read: Offset in the module, bytes, instruction: the hottest clr.dll address of the ngen load is a function's epilogue (its security cookie check, then ret 4).

tools.question: What does one call into the host, or one maths operation, cost?
tools.sample:
N 2000000, 3 rounds; ns a call is the median over the rounds; node 26.13.1, V8 14.6.202.34-node.40, branch hints read
                                this ns/call      min..max  host calls
KERNEL32.dll!lstrlenA(s:a)                24         2..27           1
KERNEL32.dll!GetACP()                    204      190..214     2000001
tools.read: ns a call over the loop without it, the spread of the rounds, and the host calls the bridge counted: lstrlenA is guest code (1 host call, the exit), GetACP crosses every time, about 200 ns. A spread wider than the median is noise: raise N.

tools.question: Where do several executors beat one?
tools.sample:
T=2 K=- H=- E=1  best3 1.55s [1.26 1.83 1.56]  x1.00 vs E=1  1807 MIPS (2.80 G)  elsewhere 0% 0 calls
T=2 K=- H=- E=2  best3 1.01s [0.96 1.32 0.77]  x1.53 vs E=1  2762 MIPS (2.80 G)  elsewhere 53% 2 calls
best of several executors: T=2 K=- H=- E=2  x1.53
tools.read: A row a point: the mean of its three fastest runs [each run], the ratio to one executor, MIPS, and the share run elsewhere. Here two threads ran 1.53 times as fast on two executors. Runs of one point that differ threefold (an earlier run of this sweep on the loaded machine gave 7.23 against 0.78 s) are the machine, not the engine: rerun on a quiet one.

tools.question: Does the translator do here the work recorded, to the unit, and how fast is it on this machine -- or how fast is one checkout against another?
tools.sample:
calls512-scatter-x87        519 MIPS  noise ±27.8 %  work as recorded
vcall-x87                  5365 MIPS  noise ±15.4 %  work as recorded
vm-x87                     3803 MIPS  noise ±1.6 %  work as recorded
calls512-scatter-x64        631 MIPS  noise ±4.8 %  work as recorded
vcall-x64                  3979 MIPS  noise ±2.7 %  work as recorded
vm-x64                     2477 MIPS  noise ±2.1 %  work as recorded
geometric mean, 32-bit: 2196 MIPS
geometric mean, 64-bit: 1839 MIPS
tools.source: node tools/bench/stand.mjs --only vm,vcall,calls512-scatter on cork 94512c08 with the stand, Node 22.22.0, a 4-core Xeon VM at 2.10 GHz, 2026-11-14
tools.read: Each workload runs on the guest's own clock, so its work (instructions, regions, every way between regions) is the same on any machine: "as recorded" is the translator doing what expected.json says; DIFFERS is the code, never the machine. MIPS is this machine's speed, the median of 7 rounds; noise is how far those rounds part (half their interquartile range): a difference inside it is not one this machine shows, and a second run can land outside it when the engine optimises otherwise (lua-x87 1290 and 2069 MIPS in two runs here). With --roots A,B a ratio column gives B against A round by round.

tools.question: Do our stdcall entries pop the bytes Windows' do?
